premise: It is tempting to think the tool call is decided only by the tool description. It isn't. The description is the main signal, but the model reads everything in its context before picking a tool, and the system prompt is part of that context. A system-prompt line such as "when the customer mentions money back, use process_refund" reads like an order from the boss, and it beats a description that reads like a label on a drawer.
diagram:
Which tool? the model reads ALL of these:
 ├ tool descriptions  ← main signal
 ├ system prompt      ← can override them
 ├ customer's words   ← trigger words
 ├ few-shot examples  ← copied patterns
 └ tool_choice        ← forces a call

evidence.quote: Each tool's schema text now lists its inputs, two sample requests and a when-not-to-use line.
evidence.means: The descriptions have already been fixed, so that lever is used up. This rules out [[0]], the runner-up, which would win only if the descriptions were still one-liners.

evidence.quote: Status questions without those words go to lookup_order correctly.
evidence.means: This proves the descriptions work. Without the trigger words, routing is fine.

evidence.quote: Every misrouted conversation contains phrases like 'money back', 'credit' or 'compensation'.
evidence.means: The mistakes track specific words, not confusion between the tools. Something is mapping those words to process_refund.

evidence.quote: The system prompt's escalation, tone and reimbursement sections were written by different teams over the past year.
evidence.means: The quiet clue. Nobody has reviewed the prompt as a whole, and its reimbursement section is the likeliest place to say "money back → refund tool".

evidence.quote: Which change is the most effective first step?
evidence.means: Reading that section is cheap and diagnostic. Splitting tools ([[1]]) or adding examples ([[3]]) changes more and treats the symptom. So [[2]].

rule: Descriptions are the main signal, not the only one. If misroutes follow specific words and the descriptions are already good, look for those words in the system prompt.

guide.quote: Ambiguous/overlapping descriptions cause misrouting; keyword-sensitive system-prompt wording creates unintended tool associations.
